newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs void $1.4 bln deal with ABB for power grid.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs void $1.4 bln deal with ABB for power grid.

text.p: Kazakhstan has annulled its $1.4 billion framework agreement with Swiss-Swedish ABB AG Power Consortium Ltd for the right to manage its national power grid for 25 years, the government announced on Thursday.
"During the talks... it became clear that the positions of the sides had led to the situation which can be qualified as an impasse," a government press release said.
ABB reached a framework concession agreement with Kazakhstan in April, less than a week after the Kazakhs said Britain's National Grid Group plc had an exclusive right to negotiate the contract.

Sarybay Kalmyrzayev, head of the finance ministry's state property department, told a news conference that ABB, which had pledged to pay wage arrears to the workers of Kazakhstan's power grid, develop a power pool and invest at least $200 million over the next three years, had not fulfilled some of the obligations.

He said that the company had not presented an internationally accepted form of guarantee for its initial $200 million investment backed by a foreign bank, and instead of an immediate takeover of the Kazakh national grid proposed to run it together with the government for the first few months.

"Taking into account the difficult situation in the power sector, there might have been some speculation, waiting until the assets of the national grid fall in price," Kalmyrzayev said. "We stick to our initial conditions...We have decided to cancel the tender results."

But Kalmyrzayev said that both ABB and National Grid could improve their offers and resume talks with the government. He said three other large foreign companies were expected to start negotiations with Kazakhstan for the right to manage its 16,000 km (10,000 miles) of power transmission lines.
